 Holiday shipments seen boosting BoC collections 
 November 16, 2026 | 9:14 pm 
 Bureau of Customs (BOC) personnel inspect balikbayan boxes in Manila. — PHILIPPINE STAR/RYAN BALDEMOR 
 FINANCE Secretary Frederick D. Go expects a surge in ship ments ahead of the holiday season to boost Bureau of Cus toms (BoC) collections and help the agency meet its P1.01-trillion full-year revenue target. 
 “We will continue to experience the seasonal high of the Bureau of Customs in the fourth quarter,” Mr. Go told reporters on the sidelines of the ASEAN Business and Investment Summit on Saturday. “I am very confident that BoC will hit the target.”
 In the January-to-October period, the BoC collected P853.66 billion, exceeding its P846.52-billion target for the period by 0.84% or P7.14 billion. This accounted for 84.44% of the agency’s P1.01-trillion target for 2026. 
 Mr. Go said recent leadership changes at the government’s main revenue agencies give him greater confidence in their reform efforts. 
 Former Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza was appointed to head the Customs bureau. He replaced former BoC Commissioner Ariel F. Nepomuceno, who was named president and chief executive officer of the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA). 
 “Now with Charlie Mendoza there… He’s very good at reforms. I must say that the reforms he instituted at the BIR were very challenging, and he was able to do it,” Mr. Go said.
 Meanwhile, Mr. Go said the BIR’s collection performance would be directly proportional to gross domestic product (GDP) growth.
 “The relationship of BIR’s growth in collections, I think, is directly correlated to the GDP growth. So, I think it’s fair to say that the BIR’s performance will be directly proportional or correlated to the growth of our country’s GDP. I think that’s the better metric to evaluate the BIR’s performance,” he said. 
 Mr. Go also expressed confidence that newly appointed BIR Commissioner Rolando T. Ligon, Jr., a former Department of Finance undersecretary, will continue to undertake the reforms started by Mr. Mendoza. 
 “We’ll have continuity and no disruption,” he added.
 The BIR collected P2.81 trillion in the January-to-October period, up 5.63% from around P2.66 trillion in the same period a year ago. This represented 82.93% of the agency’s P3.39-trillion target this year.
 Meanwhile, the Philippine economy grew by 2.5% in the first nine months of the year, well below the government’s 3.5%-4.5% full-year growth target.
 Mr. Go said his marching orders to the new BIR and Customs commissioners were to continue pursuing reforms, particularly digitalization programs.
 For the BIR, these include e-invoicing, Letter of Authority reforms, and BIR NEXT GEN, which aims to consolidate and integrate the agency’s fragmented systems into one unified platform. 
 For the BoC, these include the national single window, a new Customs processing system, and cross-border e-invoicing.
 Mr. Go said these reforms would help address corruption and improve the experience of taxpayers and other stakeholders.
 Meanwhile, the Finance chief said he had directed the new heads of the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) and BCDA to foster a business-friendly environment that would attract more foreign and domestic investment. 
 “That is the only way for us to regain our global competitiveness and to provide quality jobs for our people,” he said.
 “There’s an opportunity before us today to ride on artificial intelligence and super intelligence. So, I think we should not waste this opportunity to be able to build manufacturing facilities and build an entire ecosystem that can cater to these new technologies,” he added.
 Mr. Go said the BCDA is at the forefront of these efforts through the Luzon Economic Corridor, along with PEZA, which accredits New Clark City locators.
 “So, they really have a lot of work to do together to build this advanced manufacturing facility,” he said.
 In the first 10 months, PEZA approved P309.63 billion worth of investments by Filipino and foreign nationals, up 76.6% from P175.37 billion in the same period a year ago. 
 Meanwhile, the BCDA approved P145.46 billion worth of investments in the 10-month period, up 142.5% from P59.98 billion in the same period last year. —   Justine Irish D. Tabile
